title: Office of Public Accountability: Your Questions, Answered
description:
Who protects Angelenos when decisions are made about water and power? Meet the Office of Public Accountability (OPA), the City of Los Angeles’ official Ratepayer Advocate.

Operating independently of the Los Angeles Department of Water and Power (LADWP), OPA represents the interests of the 4 million Angelenos and nearly 250,000 businesses that depend on LADWP services. Established through a voter-approved amendment to the Los Angeles City Charter, the office promotes transparency and accountability while helping ensure LADWP delivers safe, reliable, affordable, and clean water and power.

OPA also supports the City’s goals for climate action, equity, and long-term sustainability—helping ensure that the needs of ratepayers remain at the center of important utility decisions.
